segment_text: (b) Either party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement effective upon written notice to the other party in the event the non-notifying party becomes insolvent or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or in the event bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings are instituted against the non-notifying party or on the non-notifying party's behalf.

annotator_notes:
FIRST MAY-MODALITY ITEM IN THE GOLD SET -- checked directly, no prior locked item across any batch carries this modality. Genuine termination-for-cause right with real monitorable stakes (correlative party, triggering insolvency event, written-notice mechanism), so section 2.5.1's 'no monitorable stakes' exclusion does not reach it -- this is precisely the shape section 2.5's own worked example ('Customer may terminate for cause within 30 days') describes as annotatable, unlike C04-026's unrestricted, no-correlative-party rights-reservation.

OBLIGEE -- ESCALATED, REVIEWER-RULED (new section 3.5.4, this session): 'the other party' is named in-span as both the notice recipient and the party affected by the termination, and is annotated as obligee under section 3.5's ordinary positional test -- modality does not change which field-assignment rule applies to obligor/obligee, only which value goes in modality itself. ABSENT is reserved for genuine absence of a named counterparty (C04-026's shape), not applied by default because this item is MAY rather than MUST.

OBLIGOR: 'Either party' is a distributive reference (section 3.5.1 step 1 branch 2), annotated verbatim, no accept-set -- same treatment as 'Each Party'/'the Parties' regardless of this being a MAY clause. The underlying right is symmetric (either party may terminate if the OTHER becomes insolvent), but unlike section 8.4's mutual_obligation gap (which protects against silently losing an entire SECOND duty when naming only one obligor of a MUST), naming 'Either party' verbatim already fully communicates the symmetry within the value itself -- no known_gaps tag needed for this reason.

TEMPORAL: 'effective upon written notice to the other party' is RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER, direction 'after' per section 8.9's rule (upon/following/on -> after), trigger 'written notice to the other party' verbatim. known_gaps gains relative_trigger_preposition, direct citation to section 8.9's measured table (upon <trigger>: NOT accepted by _RELATIVE_RE, 92/1547 pool segments, section 8.9's own table). underspecified=true is over-determined by trigger 3 (section 3.9) since symbols.resolve_trigger() always returns None in v1 -- both parties (Either party / the other party) are distributive/relational references that would also independently trigger underspecified per section 3.9 trigger 1, but missing_fields lists only temporal.trigger since that's the field typecheck.py actually appends for an unresolved TriggerRef; the party references are annotated verbatim per section 3.5.1 branch 2 without a resolve_party() failure being the operative mechanism here (no individual name is being looked up at all).

CONDITIONS: one entry, the whole 'in the event...on the non-notifying party's behalf' clause verbatim, internal 'or's unparsed per section 17.2/section 3.8 (do not split a single condition string on internal AND/OR).

ACTION/OBJECT: TERMINATE is an exact taxonomy match. object_class 'agreement' is a single-anchor object (no dual-anchor consideration needed, unlike C11-01's possessor/thing-owned case).
